question: In a left occiput anterior presentation, the cardinal movement of internal rotation brings the occiput from the left anterior position to directly under the symphysis pubis.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. This statement is true. Internal rotation does bring the occiput of an LOA fetus to the direct anterior (OA) position under the symphysis pubis, aligning the longest head diameter with the widest AP outlet diameter.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Internal rotation turns the head so the occiput rotates anteriorly to lie directly behind the symphysis pubis (the position of least resistance through the mid-pelvis and outlet). In LOA, this is a 45-degree medial rotation.
